t: The Romans fought with two legions in the centre and allied infantry on the flanks, and the Macedonians with a pike phalanx and an elite guard of 3,000.
The phalanx lost its cohesion as it advanced over rough ground in the foothills, and Paullus ordered the legions into the gaps to attack the phalangites on their exposed flanks.
Perseus was later paraded in triumph in Rome in chains, the Macedonian kingdom was dissolved into four republics, and Macedonia in time became a Roman province.
dyk: The night before the battle there was a lunar eclipse, which the Macedonians perceived as an ill omen; according to Plutarch, they took it as a sign of their king's demise.
ev: The Third Macedonian War starts after acts by King Perseus of Macedon lead Rome to declare war
Perseus wins the Battle of Callinicus and regains most of his losses, including the city of Dion
Lucius Aemilius Paullus takes command of the Roman force and sends Scipio Nasica on a march round the Macedonian position
Perseus withdraws north to a plain near Katerini, south of Pydna, suited to the phalanx
The Roman legions break the Macedonian phalanx at Pydna and the pursuit lasts until nightfall
Perseus later surrenders to Paullus and is taken to Rome and paraded in triumph in chains
Paullus attacks Epirus, enslaving 150,000 Epirotes and sacking 70 cities

f.date: 22 June 168 BCE; the fighting began in the afternoon
f.place: A fairly level plain near Katerini, a village south of Pydna, below the foothills of Mount Olocrus in Macedonia, northern Greece
f.sides: Rome and its allies under the consul Lucius Aemilius Paullus, at least 28,600 men and up to 37,000; Macedon under King Perseus, 43,000 soldiers at the start of the war and closer to 30,000 by the time of the battle
f.outcome: The Roman legions broke the Macedonian phalanx; Perseus fled, nearly 11,000 Macedonians were captured, and Livy reported that his sources claimed up to 20,000 Macedonian dead.
